Local presence along a tree: the dynamic null model of DAMOCLES

Source: R/damocles.R
simulate_damocles.Rd

simulate_damocles() simulates the presence and absence of each lineage of a clade in one local community, as it diversifies along tree, under the dynamic null model of community assembly of Pigot & Etienne (2015), DAMOCLES. Along each branch the lineage is either locally absent (state 0) or present (state 1); an absent lineage colonises the community at rate gamma and a present one goes locally extinct at rate mu, the same for every lineage unless rates are given for each edge. At each speciation, which is allopatric, a locally present ancestor leaves one daughter present and the other absent, chosen at random, and an absent ancestor leaves two absent daughters. The states at the tips form the community.

Usage

simulate_damocles(
  tree,
  gamma,
  mu,
  n = 1,
  root = c("both", "absent", "present"),
  sympatry = 0
)

Arguments

tree

A rooted, fully dichotomous phylo tree with branch lengths.

gamma

Rate of local colonisation per lineage, in the units of the branch lengths: one rate, or one per edge of tree in the order of tree$edge.

mu

Rate of local extinction per lineage, one or one per edge. With rates per edge and a root edge, the two edges leaving the root must have the same rates, which the root edge takes.

n

Number of communities to simulate.

root

State of the ancestor at the root, just before the first speciation (or at the start of the root edge): "both" draws absent or present with equal probabilities for each community, as in the simulations of Pigot & Etienne (2015); "absent" or "present" fix it.

sympatry

Probability, between 0 and 1, that a locally present ancestor leaves both daughters present at speciation; 0 (the default) is strictly allopatric speciation.

Value

A matrix of zeros and ones with one row per community and one column per tip, named by the tips, ready to be used as comm in the other functions of the package.

Details

sympatry relaxes the rule of strictly allopatric speciation: with that probability a present ancestor leaves both daughters present, as after speciation within the community (in situ or sympatric speciation) or when one daughter recolonises it before the two can be told apart; otherwise one daughter is present, as above. sympatry = 0, the default, is the model of Pigot & Etienne (2015). An absent ancestor always leaves two absent daughters.

The states at the nodes are drawn from the exact transition probabilities of the two-state process over each branch, which gives the same distribution of tip states as simulating each colonisation and extinction event. The model assumes the tree holds the species of the regional pool, so it is meant for ultrametric trees of extant species. Branches of length zero and a root edge (tree$root.edge) are allowed.

References

Pigot, A. L., & Etienne, R. S. (2015). A new dynamic null model for phylogenetic community structure. Ecology Letters, 18, 153–163. doi:10.1111/ele.12395

See also

damocles_loglik() and damocles_fit() for the likelihood, damocles_test() for the null model of phylogenetic community structure.

Other dynamic null model: clade_regimes(), confint.mc_damocles_fit(), damocles_loglik(), damocles_lrt(), damocles_test()

Examples

set.seed(1)
tr <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(30)
comm <- simulate_damocles(tr, gamma = 0.5, mu = 0.5, n = 5)
rowSums(comm)
#> sim1 sim2 sim3 sim4 sim5 
#>    4    4    2    6    3
